spec.description: Animals on the move, from three open datasets: lesser black-backed gulls from Zeebrugge (INBO), jaguars across the Neotropics (Jaguar Movement Database) and sharks, tunas, whales, seals and turtles of the Pacific (TOPP, Animal Telemetry Network). Animated trails, distances and who went farthest.

options.content:
### About the data
Three open datasets of animals tracked by GPS or satellite, each read where it is published, through the stack's gateway, which keeps a copy for a month: none of them changes. DuckDB on the server reads each one once per visit and hands the browser a thinned copy; [Chaski](https://github.com/ubica-ecuador/chaski) runs every query on the page there.

| Tab | Dataset | Publisher | Licence | Here |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gulls | [LBBG_ADULT – Lesser black-backed gulls breeding in Belgium](https://zenodo.org/records/22083084) (2022–2025) | INBO, Research Institute for Nature and Forest; Movebank study, Zenodo | CC0 1.0 | One position per bird every two hours; kilometres from every fix |
| Jaguars | [Jaguar Movement Database](https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.2dh0223), Morato et al. 2018, *Ecology* 99: 1691 | 20 research projects; Dryad, Zenodo copy | CC0 1.0 | One position per jaguar every two hours |
| Ocean | [IOOS ATN Trackline Database, Stanford Block Lab](https://atn.ioos.us/erddap/tabledap/stanford_import_ssm_public.html) (TOPP, 2002–2018) | Animal Telemetry Network, NOAA IOOS, on ERDDAP | Free use and redistribution, not for legal use | Tracks smoothed by a state-space model; one position per animal and day |

**Distances** are straight lines between fixes on a sphere, so they are a floor on what an animal travelled; fewer fixes, a lower floor. **The gulls' colony** is the median of all their positions in June. **Ocean longitudes** past 100°E are moved 360° west, so tracks across the date line draw as one line on a Pacific map.

**Not here:** the jaguars' sex, age and weight ship in the same archive as a spreadsheet misnamed `.csv`, which the reader cannot open from inside the ZIP. Movebank, the largest store of animal tracks, needs an account to download, so only studies also published on Zenodo or Dryad can join.

spec.rawSql:
-- One row per bird within the window, time of day and month picked, the
-- farthest travellers first, under a row for all of them, whose click lets the
-- bird followed go.
WITH w AS (
  SELECT coalesce(nullif($g_lo, ''), '01-01') AS lo, coalesce(nullif($g_hi, ''), '12-31') AS hi,
         try_cast($g_hour AS INTEGER) AS hr, try_cast($g_month AS INTEGER) AS mo
),
b AS (
  SELECT bird, max(colony_km) AS far, min(latitude) AS south, sum(km) AS km,
         sum(fixes) AS fixes, min(time) AS t0, max(time) AS t1
  FROM $gulls, w
  WHERE strftime(time, '%m-%d') BETWEEN w.lo AND w.hi
  AND (w.hr IS NULL OR hour(time) // 2 * 2 = w.hr)
  AND (w.mo IS NULL OR month(time) = w.mo)
  GROUP BY bird
),
rows AS (
  SELECT 0 AS o, 'All birds' AS label, '' AS bird, max(far) AS far, min(south) AS south,
         sum(km) AS km, sum(fixes) AS fixes, min(t0) AS t0, max(t1) AS t1
  FROM b
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 1, bird, bird, far, south, km, fixes, t0, t1 FROM b
)
SELECT label                           AS "Bird",
       round(far)                      AS "Farthest, km",
       round(south, 1)                 AS "Southernmost, °N",
       round(km)                       AS "Km flown",
       fixes                           AS "GPS fixes",
       strftime(t0, '%Y-%m-%d')        AS "First fix",
       strftime(t1, '%Y-%m-%d')        AS "Last fix",
       bird                            AS bird_id
FROM rows
ORDER BY o, far DESC

spec.description: Within the window, time of day and month picked. Click a bird to follow it alone; All birds brings the others back.
spec.title: Birds

spec.rawSql:
-- How far each bird got from the colony, day by day: its farthest position
-- that day. The colony is the median of every position in June. The whole
-- year, whatever the window: the window is picked here.
SELECT time_bucket(INTERVAL 1 DAY, time) AS time, bird AS name, max(colony_km) AS value
FROM $gulls
WHERE ($bird = '' OR bird = $bird)
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY name, time

spec.description: Each bird's farthest position from the colony, day by day; the colony is the median of all the birds' positions in June. Click a line to follow that bird, and again to let it go. The brush at the top right picks a window of days for the map, the figures and the table. The bar is the map's clock.
spec.title: Distance from the colony

spec.rawSql:
-- Kilometres flown by two-hour block (UTC) and month, within the window and
-- for the bird followed; not narrowed by the cell picked here.
WITH w AS (
  SELECT coalesce(nullif($g_lo, ''), '01-01') AS lo, coalesce(nullif($g_hi, ''), '12-31') AS hi,
         try_cast($g_hour AS INTEGER) AS hr, try_cast($g_month AS INTEGER) AS mo
)
SELECT month(time) AS month, hour(time) // 2 * 2 AS hour, round(sum(km)) AS value
FROM $gulls, w
WHERE ($bird = '' OR bird = $bird)
  AND strftime(time, '%m-%d') BETWEEN w.lo AND w.hi
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY month, hour

spec.description: Kilometres flown in each two-hour block of the day (UTC; Belgium is one or two hours ahead) and each month. Click a cell to keep that block of that month on the map, the figures and the table; click an hour or a month on the axes to keep it alone; click again to let go.
spec.title: When they fly

options.content:
### Lesser black-backed gulls from Zeebrugge
Gulls GPS-tagged by [INBO](https://www.inbo.be/en) at their colony in the port of Zeebrugge, Belgium: up to 33 birds a year, a fix every few minutes, some wintering at home and some flying on to Iberia, Morocco or Mauritania. **Press play** on the map's clock to watch the year go by; the bar on *Distance from the colony* follows it, and hovering the chart shows on the map where every bird was then. **Click a line** (or a bird in the table) to follow one bird; **pick a window of days** with the brush at the chart's top right, say the autumn migration; **click a cell** of *When they fly* for one time of day in one month. *Gull year* picks the year.

spec.rawSql:
-- Every bird, or the one followed, within the window, time of day and month
-- picked; trip_id groups a bird's positions, one every two hours, into a trail.
WITH w AS (
  SELECT coalesce(nullif($g_lo, ''), '01-01') AS lo, coalesce(nullif($g_hi, ''), '12-31') AS hi,
         try_cast($g_hour AS INTEGER) AS hr, try_cast($g_month AS INTEGER) AS mo
)
SELECT bird AS trip_id, time, latitude, longitude, colony_km, km
FROM $gulls, w
WHERE ($bird = '' OR bird = $bird)
  AND strftime(time, '%m-%d') BETWEEN w.lo AND w.hi
  AND (w.hr IS NULL OR hour(time) // 2 * 2 = w.hr)
  AND (w.mo IS NULL OR month(time) = w.mo)
ORDER BY bird, time

WITH w AS (
  SELECT coalesce(nullif($g_lo, ''), '01-01') AS lo, coalesce(nullif($g_hi, ''), '12-31') AS hi,
         try_cast($g_hour AS INTEGER) AS hr, try_cast($g_month AS INTEGER) AS mo
)
SELECT count(DISTINCT bird)          AS "Birds",
       sum(fixes)                    AS "GPS fixes",
       round(sum(km))                AS "Km flown",
       round(max(colony_km))         AS "Farthest, km"
FROM $gulls, w
WHERE ($bird = '' OR bird = $bird)
  AND strftime(time, '%m-%d') BETWEEN w.lo AND w.hi
  AND (w.hr IS NULL OR hour(time) // 2 * 2 = w.hr)
  AND (w.mo IS NULL OR month(time) = w.mo)

spec.description: Within the window, time of day and month picked. Km flown adds up every fix to the next, before the map's thinning to one position every two hours. Farthest is from the colony.

spec.rawSql:
-- With a jaguar followed: the kilometres between its fixes, day by day.
-- Without: each country's median day, month by month. Every country, whatever
-- the legend says: the legend is where they are left out.
WITH d AS (
  SELECT jaguar, country, time_bucket(INTERVAL 1 DAY, time) AS day, any_value(day_km) AS km
  FROM $jaguars
  GROUP BY ALL
)
SELECT day AS time, jaguar AS name, round(km, 2) AS value
FROM d WHERE $jaguar <> '' AND jaguar = $jaguar
UNION ALL
SELECT time_bucket(INTERVAL 1 MONTH, day) AS time, country AS name, round(median(km), 2) AS value
FROM d WHERE $jaguar = ''
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY name, time

spec.description: Each country's median day, month by month, or the jaguar followed day by day. Click a country in the legend to leave it out of the map, the figures and the tables; click the line of the jaguar followed to let it go. The bar is the map's clock.
spec.title: Distance walked per day

spec.rawSql:
-- Jaguar-days by kilometres walked between fixes, in 1 km bars, the last one
-- 30 km and over; for the jaguar followed and the countries left, not
-- narrowed by the range picked here.
WITH w AS (SELECT string_split($j_off, ',') AS off),
d AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT jaguar, time::DATE AS day, day_km
  FROM $jaguars, w
  WHERE ($jaguar = '' OR jaguar = $jaguar) AND NOT list_contains(w.off, country)
)
SELECT b.bin, count(d.day) AS n
FROM range(0, 31) AS b(bin)
LEFT JOIN d ON least(floor(d.day_km), 30) = b.bin
GROUP BY b.bin
ORDER BY b.bin

spec.description: How many jaguar-days walked each distance, in kilometres between fixes. Drag across it to keep only those days on the map, the figures and the tables; the toolbox clears it.
spec.title: Kilometres a day

options.content:
### Jaguars of the Neotropics
The [Jaguar Movement Database](https://doi.org/10.1002/ecy.2379): 117 jaguars GPS-collared by 20 projects from Sonora to Argentina between 1999 and 2016, most of them in Brazil's and Paraguay's Pantanal, where the map opens. Each trail is a week long; **press play** and the bar on *Distance walked per day* follows the clock. **Drag across** *Kilometres a day* to keep only the days of long walks, or the quiet ones; **click a country** in the chart's legend to leave it out; **click a study area** to fly there, or **a jaguar** (or its line) to follow it alone.

spec.rawSql:
-- One row per jaguar, the longest walkers first, under a row for all of
-- them, whose click lets the jaguar followed go.
WITH w AS (
  SELECT string_split($j_off, ',') AS off,
         coalesce(try_cast($j_lo AS DOUBLE), 0) AS lo,
         coalesce(try_cast($j_hi AS DOUBLE), 'infinity'::DOUBLE) AS hi
),
j AS (
  SELECT jaguar, any_value(study) AS study, any_value(country) AS country,
         min(time) AS t0, max(time) AS t1, count(DISTINCT time::DATE) AS jdays,
         sum(fixes) AS fixes, sum(km) AS km, median(latitude) AS lat, median(longitude) AS lng
  FROM $jaguars, w
  WHERE NOT list_contains(w.off, country)
  AND day_km >= w.lo AND day_km < w.hi
  GROUP BY jaguar
),
rows AS (
  SELECT 0 AS o, 'All jaguars' AS label, '' AS jaguar, '' AS study, '' AS country,
         min(t0) AS t0, max(t1) AS t1, sum(jdays) AS jdays, sum(fixes) AS fixes, sum(km) AS km,
         NULL::DOUBLE AS lat, NULL::DOUBLE AS lng
  FROM j
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 1, jaguar, jaguar, study, country, t0, t1, jdays, fixes, km, lat, lng FROM j
)
SELECT label                              AS "Jaguar",
       study                              AS "Study area",
       country                            AS "Country",
       strftime(t0, '%Y-%m-%d')           AS "First fix",
       strftime(t1, '%Y-%m-%d')           AS "Last fix",
       jdays                              AS "Days",
       fixes                              AS "GPS fixes",
       round(km)                          AS "Km walked",
       round(km / greatest(jdays, 1), 1)  AS "Km a day",
       jaguar                             AS jaguar_id,
       round(lat, 4)                      AS lat,
       round(lng, 4)                      AS lng
FROM rows
ORDER BY o, km DESC

spec.description: In the countries left and within the range of kilometres a day picked. Click a jaguar to follow it alone, and the map flies to it; All jaguars brings the others back.
spec.title: Jaguars

spec.rawSql:
-- Every jaguar, or the one followed, in the countries left and on the days
-- within the range of kilometres picked; one position every two hours at most.
-- With a range picked, each day is a trail of its own, so the days left out
-- are not drawn as jumps. Coloured by country.
WITH w AS (
  SELECT string_split($j_off, ',') AS off,
         coalesce(try_cast($j_lo AS DOUBLE), 0) AS lo,
         coalesce(try_cast($j_hi AS DOUBLE), 'infinity'::DOUBLE) AS hi
)
SELECT CASE WHEN w.lo = 0 AND w.hi = 'infinity'::DOUBLE THEN jaguar
            ELSE jaguar || ' ' || strftime(time, '%Y-%m-%d') END AS trip_id,
       jaguar, study, country, time, latitude, longitude, day_km
FROM $jaguars, w
WHERE ($jaguar = '' OR jaguar = $jaguar)
  AND NOT list_contains(w.off, country)
  AND day_km >= w.lo AND day_km < w.hi
ORDER BY trip_id, time

WITH w AS (
  SELECT string_split($j_off, ',') AS off,
         coalesce(try_cast($j_lo AS DOUBLE), 0) AS lo,
         coalesce(try_cast($j_hi AS DOUBLE), 'infinity'::DOUBLE) AS hi
)
SELECT count(DISTINCT jaguar)                      AS "Jaguars",
       count(DISTINCT (jaguar, time::DATE))        AS "Jaguar-days",
       round(sum(km))                              AS "Km walked",
       count(DISTINCT study)                       AS "Study areas"
FROM $jaguars, w
WHERE ($jaguar = '' OR jaguar = $jaguar)
  AND NOT list_contains(w.off, country)
  AND day_km >= w.lo AND day_km < w.hi

spec.description: In the countries left and within the range of kilometres a day picked. Km walked adds up the straight lines between fixes, so it is a floor: a jaguar walks more than that, and some collars fixed hours apart.

spec.rawSql:
-- One row per project, the largest first; a click flies the map to it.
WITH w AS (
  SELECT string_split($j_off, ',') AS off,
         coalesce(try_cast($j_lo AS DOUBLE), 0) AS lo,
         coalesce(try_cast($j_hi AS DOUBLE), 'infinity'::DOUBLE) AS hi
)
SELECT study                                  AS "Study area",
       any_value(country)                     AS "Country",
       count(DISTINCT jaguar)                 AS "Jaguars",
       sum(fixes)                             AS "GPS fixes",
       min(year(time)) || '–' || max(year(time)) AS "Years",
       round(median(latitude), 4)             AS lat,
       round(median(longitude), 4)            AS lng
FROM $jaguars, w
WHERE NOT list_contains(w.off, country)
  AND day_km >= w.lo AND day_km < w.hi
GROUP BY study
ORDER BY "GPS fixes" DESC

spec.description: In the countries left and within the range of kilometres a day picked. Click a study area to fly the map to it.
spec.title: Study areas

options.content:
### Ocean predators of the Pacific
[Tagging of Pacific Predators](https://gtopp.org/) (TOPP): 1,243 sharks, tunas, whales, seals, turtles and seabirds of 30 species tagged by the Stanford Block Lab from 2002 to 2018, one position a day, from the [Animal Telemetry Network](https://ioos.noaa.gov/project/atn/). Pick species in *Ocean species*; each trail is a month long, and **press play** to see the bar on *Latitude through the year* follow the season. **Click a month** on that chart to keep it alone, every year of it: blue whales north in summer, south in winter. **Click a species** in its legend to leave it out, and **a tag** in the table to follow one animal.

spec.rawSql:
-- Where each species spends the year: the median latitude of its daily
-- positions, month by month, every year together. Every species and month,
-- whatever is picked: both are picked here.
SELECT month(time) AS month, species AS name, round(median(latitude), 1) AS value
FROM $ocean
WHERE ($tag = '' OR tag = $tag)
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY name, month

spec.description: The median latitude of each species' daily positions, month by month, every year together: the seasons of a migration. Click a month to keep it alone on the map, the figures and the table, and again to let it go; click a species in the legend to leave it out. The solid bar is the month the map is playing.
spec.title: Latitude through the year

spec.rawSql:
-- The species picked and left in the legend, or the one animal followed, in
-- the month picked; one position a day, longitudes past 100°E moved 360° west
-- so the Pacific stays in one piece. With a month picked, each year's is a
-- trail of its own, so the rest of the year is not drawn as one jump.
WITH w AS (
  SELECT string_split($o_off, ',') AS off, try_cast($o_month AS INTEGER) AS mo
)
SELECT CASE WHEN w.mo IS NULL THEN tag ELSE tag || ' ' || year(time) END AS trip_id,
       tag, species, time, latitude, longitude, km
FROM $ocean, w
WHERE ($tag = '' OR tag = $tag)
  AND NOT list_contains(w.off, species)
  AND (w.mo IS NULL OR month(time) = w.mo)
ORDER BY trip_id, time

-- Every species TOPP tagged, the most tagged first: what there is to pick.
SELECT species                                  AS "Species",
       taxon                                    AS "Group",
       tags                                     AS "Animals",
       positions                                AS "Positions",
       first_year || '–' || last_year           AS "Years"
FROM $ocean_species
ORDER BY tags DESC

spec.description: Every species in TOPP, picked or not: what there is to pick in Ocean species.
spec.title: What TOPP tagged

spec.rawSql:
WITH w AS (
  SELECT string_split($o_off, ',') AS off, try_cast($o_month AS INTEGER) AS mo
)
SELECT count(DISTINCT tag)      AS "Animals",
       count(*)                 AS "Positions",
       round(sum(km))           AS "Km travelled",
       count(DISTINCT species)  AS "Species"
FROM $ocean, w
WHERE ($tag = '' OR tag = $tag)
  AND NOT list_contains(w.off, species)
  AND (w.mo IS NULL OR month(time) = w.mo)

spec.description: The species left in the legend, in the month picked. One position per animal and day; Km travelled adds up the straight lines between them.

spec.rawSql:
-- One row per animal of the species left, in the month picked, the longest
-- journeys first, under a row for all of them, whose click lets the animal
-- followed go.
WITH w AS (
  SELECT string_split($o_off, ',') AS off, try_cast($o_month AS INTEGER) AS mo
),
t AS (
  SELECT tag, any_value(species) AS species, min(time) AS t0, max(time) AS t1,
         count(*) AS positions, sum(km) AS km, max(latitude) AS north, min(latitude) AS south
  FROM $ocean, w
  WHERE NOT list_contains(w.off, species)
  AND (w.mo IS NULL OR month(time) = w.mo)
  GROUP BY tag
),
rows AS (
  SELECT 0 AS o, 'All tags' AS label, '' AS tag, '' AS species, min(t0) AS t0, max(t1) AS t1,
         sum(positions) AS positions, sum(km) AS km, max(north) AS north, min(south) AS south
  FROM t
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 1, tag, tag, species, t0, t1, positions, km, north, south FROM t
)
SELECT label                              AS "Tag",
       species                            AS "Species",
       strftime(t0, '%Y-%m-%d')           AS "First position",
       strftime(t1, '%Y-%m-%d')           AS "Last position",
       positions                          AS "Positions",
       round(km)                          AS "Km travelled",
       round(north, 1) + 0.0              AS "Northernmost, °N",
       round(south, 1) + 0.0              AS "Southernmost, °N",
       tag                                AS tag_id
FROM rows
ORDER BY o, km DESC

spec.description: The species left, in the month picked. Click a tag to follow that animal alone on the map; All tags brings the others back.
spec.title: Tags
Animals on the move

spec.description: The year of the gulls on the first tab; INBO publishes one file a year.
spec.label: Gull year
spec.name: year

query.rawSql:
-- Server side, once per visit and per year picked: the lesser black-backed
-- gulls INBO tags at their colony in the port of Zeebrugge (Belgium), from
-- the Zenodo copy of the Movebank study LBBG_ADULT (CC0), read through the
-- gateway's month-long cache. A year is up to 2 million GPS fixes, minutes
-- apart; the browser gets one position per bird every two hours, with the
-- fixes and the kilometres flown in those two hours, measured fix to fix.
WITH raw AS (
  SELECT "individual-local-identifier" AS bird, timestamp AS t,
         "location-lat" AS lat, "location-long" AS lon
  FROM read_csv('http://feeds/zenodo/records/22083084/files/LBBG_ADULT-gps-${year:raw}.csv.gz')
  WHERE visible AND "location-lat" IS NOT NULL AND "location-long" IS NOT NULL
),
leg AS (
  SELECT *, 2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(
           pow(sin(radians(lat - lag(lat) OVER w) / 2), 2)
           + cos(radians(lat)) * cos(radians(lag(lat) OVER w)) * pow(sin(radians(lon - lag(lon) OVER w) / 2), 2))) AS km
  FROM raw WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY bird ORDER BY t)
),
slot AS (
  SELECT bird, min(t) AS time, arg_min(lat, t) AS lat, arg_min(lon, t) AS lon,
         count(*) AS fixes, coalesce(sum(km), 0) AS km
  FROM leg GROUP BY bird, time_bucket(INTERVAL 2 HOUR, t)
),
-- The colony: the median of every bird's positions in June, mid-breeding.
colony AS (SELECT median(lat) AS clat, median(lon) AS clon FROM slot WHERE month(time) = 6)
SELECT bird, time,
       round(lat, 5) AS latitude, round(lon, 5) AS longitude,
       fixes, round(km, 3) AS km,
       round(2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(
         pow(sin(radians(lat - clat) / 2), 2)
         + cos(radians(lat)) * cos(radians(clat)) * pow(sin(radians(lon - clon) / 2), 2))), 1) AS colony_km
FROM slot CROSS JOIN colony
ORDER BY bird, time

-- Server side, once per visit: the Jaguar Movement Database (Morato et al.
-- 2018, Ecology; CC0), 117 jaguars GPS-collared by 20 projects from Mexico to
-- Argentina, 1999 to 2016. Zenodo has it as a ZIP: GDAL reads the CSV inside
-- it by ranges of the gateway's month-long cached copy. Timestamps are local
-- and month/day/two-digit year. One position per jaguar every two hours, with
-- the fixes and the kilometres between fixes in those two hours, and the
-- kilometres of the whole day (day_km), which the dashboard filters days on.
WITH raw AS (
  SELECT "individual.local.identifier (ID)" AS jaguar,
         trim(regexp_replace("study.name", '^[Jj]aguar_', '')) AS study,
         country,
         strptime(timestamp, '%m/%d/%y %H:%M') AS t,
         "location.lat"::DOUBLE AS lat, "location.long"::DOUBLE AS lon
  FROM ST_Read('/vsizip//vsicurl/http://feeds/zenodo/records/5001568/files/DataS1.zip/DataS1/jaguar_movement_data.csv')
),
leg AS (
  SELECT *, 2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(
           pow(sin(radians(lat - lag(lat) OVER w) / 2), 2)
           + cos(radians(lat)) * cos(radians(lag(lat) OVER w)) * pow(sin(radians(lon - lag(lon) OVER w) / 2), 2))) AS km
  FROM raw WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY jaguar ORDER BY t)
),
slot AS (
  SELECT 'J' || lpad(jaguar, 3, '0') AS jaguar, any_value(study) AS study, any_value(country) AS country,
         min(t) AS time, round(arg_min(lat, t), 5) AS latitude, round(arg_min(lon, t), 5) AS longitude,
         count(*) AS fixes, coalesce(sum(km), 0) AS km
  FROM leg
  GROUP BY jaguar, time_bucket(INTERVAL 2 HOUR, t)
)
SELECT jaguar, study, country, time, latitude, longitude, fixes, round(km, 3) AS km,
       round(sum(km) OVER (PARTITION BY jaguar, time::DATE), 2) AS day_km
FROM slot
ORDER BY jaguar, time

-- Server side, once per visit: what TOPP tagged, species by species, from the
-- same cached table as the tracks below.
SELECT species, taxon, count(DISTINCT tag) AS tags, count(*) AS positions,
       min(year(time)) AS first_year, max(year(time)) AS last_year
FROM read_csv('http://feeds/atn/topp.csv', header = false,
              columns = {'time': 'TIMESTAMPTZ', 'latitude': 'DOUBLE', 'longitude': 'DOUBLE',
                         'species': 'VARCHAR', 'tag': 'BIGINT', 'taxon': 'VARCHAR'})
GROUP BY species, taxon
ORDER BY tags DESC

spec.description: The species on the Ocean predators tab, the most tagged first.
spec.label: Ocean species
spec.name: species

spec.sql:
-- Every species TOPP tagged, the most tagged first.
SELECT species FROM $ocean_species ORDER BY tags DESC

query.rawSql:
-- Server side, once per visit and per choice of species: Tagging of Pacific
-- Predators (TOPP), the Stanford Block Lab's satellite and archival tags,
-- 2002 to 2018, as the Animal Telemetry Network publishes it on ERDDAP: tracks
-- already smoothed by a state-space model, about one position a day. Read
-- through the gateway's month-long cache. One position per animal and day,
-- with the kilometres covered since the previous one. West of 100°E a
-- longitude moves 360° west, so a crossing of the date line stays one line on
-- a Pacific-centred map instead of a stroke across the whole world.
WITH raw AS (
  SELECT tag, species, taxon, timezone('UTC', time) AS t, latitude AS lat, longitude AS lon
  FROM read_csv('http://feeds/atn/topp.csv', header = false,
                columns = {'time': 'TIMESTAMPTZ', 'latitude': 'DOUBLE', 'longitude': 'DOUBLE',
                           'species': 'VARCHAR', 'tag': 'BIGINT', 'taxon': 'VARCHAR'})
  WHERE species IN (${species:sqlstring}) AND lat IS NOT NULL AND lon IS NOT NULL
),
day AS (
  SELECT tag, any_value(species) AS species, any_value(taxon) AS taxon,
         min(t) AS time, arg_min(lat, t) AS lat, arg_min(lon, t) AS lon
  FROM raw GROUP BY tag, t::DATE
)
SELECT tag::VARCHAR AS tag, species, taxon, time,
       round(lat, 4) AS latitude,
       round(CASE WHEN lon > 100 THEN lon - 360 ELSE lon END, 4) AS longitude,
       round(coalesce(2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(
         pow(sin(radians(lat - lag(lat) OVER w) / 2), 2)
         + cos(radians(lat)) * cos(radians(lag(lat) OVER w)) * pow(sin(radians(lon - lag(lon) OVER w) / 2), 2))), 0), 2) AS km
FROM day
WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY tag ORDER BY time)
ORDER BY tag, time
